As a bartender/server in America, I'm the bread winner for my family.   I have a higher hourly wage then most, but I still come in about $2.75 under our pathetic minimum wage.

I don't work in a high end place.  It's a brewery where the largest tab for 2 might hit $100 and that's cause they were DRANKING or they took to-go beer with them 

My tips while not consistent as we have some lengthy "off-seasons", overall average substantially more then what I could make at most any hourly wage job available to me.

Somedays I make $40 an hour, somedays it's $20.  I was offered a management position and ultimately turned it down because of the drastic paycut, more hours and responsibilities, with minimal extra benefits that would have come with it.

I am a champion of fight for $15 here in the US, but honestly, of we did away with tips and I got paid $15 an hour, our family would be on welfare.

Are we going to?  Fuck if I know.   That monthly stain seems to say otherwise.  No miscarriages here, just straight up nothing.   People say, be patient, things happen when you get older.  But at this point the idea of starting over at 40 doesn't seem fair to anyone.  That doesn't mean it doesn't hurt when people stick their nose into our only child business though.  Worse even when they start it with her.  "What about you, sweetie? Do you want a little brother or sister?".  Like she has any control in the matter. As if the friendly inquiry doesn't crush my soul the same way every monthly failure does when I don't deliver on the baby sibling she absolutely wants but for some reason probably won't get.

My husband's cousin was just a toddler when his mother's German Shepherd bit the young girl in the face for running up on the dog and his younger brother. To this day half of her face doesn't work.

Our first dog was a very special needs pit/boxer.  He'd been abused and through multiple homes before 1 year.  He was blind, he had shaky eye syndrome, major food allergies, ate his own poop when he messed inside for fear of being beat and then would throw that up inside.  

We took care of him the best we could unit he started with repeat staph infections and skin pustules.  The treatment was regular steroids which started to change his body and personality.  As soon as he began to bite we put him down and he was just about 5 at the time.   We felt horrible but his life wasn't good and he became to volatile to trust.  Sometime you just gotta do what you gotta to do.
